content.comment_body: Hello everyone, If you want to use the Android app to connect to a [product_name] [article_no], it works smoothly on your local network, but accessing it remotely can lead to various errors. Based on my experience, if you see a message like "ERROR SSL Handshaking Failed," you should review your port mapping settings and assign port 8080 within your LAN. For example, if you're using a dynamic DNS service, [your_ddns].dyndns.org > [your_ip] In your router’s configuration menu, under port mapping, add an entry like this: Entry port: (your choice) LAN port: 8080 LAN IP: IP address of your [product_name] on the local network Hope this helps :-)

analysis.insight_summary: Users trying to remotely access a [product_name] controller through an Android app often experience 'SSL Handshaking Failed' errors outside their local network. This issue demonstrates the importance of proper network and port mapping settings for secure and consistent remote access. The feedback reveals a need for clearer setup instructions regarding port mapping and network security when accessing devices remotely.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects simple and reliable remote access to the [product_name] controller using the Android app, without facing SSL or connection issues.
